- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias of 2–5% in subsequent periods.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model frequently underestimates; add 1–3% upward bias to compensate.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if price is trending sharply upward, forecast often peaks too early; adjust downward 1–2% in next 2–3 periods.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days) — apply 2–4% downward correction for first 5 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated high-low swings, model fails to capture volatility — use sentiment-weighted smoothing: average sentiment over last 5 days to adjust forecast volatility.
